identity: Singer and film actor · United States · 1935–1977
title: Elvis Presley's birth chart
metaDescription: Elvis Presley's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.6° Capricorn. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, the Sun holds a sextile to Jupiter at 0.6° — close enough to weld identity to expansion. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 17.6° into Capricorn — the second decan, which the old scheme hands to Venus. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: The personal planets sit Mercury at 22.8° Capricorn, Mars at 13.0° Libra. Mercury in an earth sign reads as thought with its feet on the ground; Mars in an air sign reads as effort aimed through strategy and words.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun sextile Jupiter, 0.6° of separation. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Saturn sextile Uranus at 1.7°, and Venus square Uranus at 2.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mercury opposes Pluto while both square Uranus. Two squares braced against one opposition make a t-square — the chart’s working end, where pressure keeps finding the same outlet. The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The dignity table, which predates the outer planets and only ever spoke for seven, marks two placements here. Mars in Libra at 13.0° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Saturn in Aquarius at 25.8° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Balance, counted honestly across the 8 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: elements earth 3, air 2, water 2, fire 1; modalities cardinal 5, fixed 2, mutable 1. Venus crossed from Capricorn into Aquarius during that day, so its sign is left open. Neptune and Pluto were retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Aquarius into Pisces during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.7° between one midnight and the next. Half the day belongs to each sign, and the split falls at an unrecorded hour — so this page holds the Moon as a genuine unknown.
